issues.title: Production and authenticated product are not verified
issues.description: No production crawl or lawful signed-in storage state was supplied. Local rendering cannot establish production configuration, tenant isolation, paid entitlements, real provider behavior, or returning-user data states.
issues.evidence: Local preview and signed-out routes were exercised; productionVerified is false throughout. playwright.release.config.ts requires KOVA_RELEASE_AUTH_STATE for authenticated coverage.
issues.userImpact: Release readiness and signed-in claims remain unproven.
issues.recommendedFix: Run the same matrix against a staging release candidate using seeded free/Plus/Pro owner/editor/viewer accounts, then separately run non-mutating production smoke checks.

issues.title: Long-running execution is explicitly unavailable
issues.description: The rendered product can show history, but creation/control cannot be completed because the agent runner is disabled.
issues.evidence: The route states “Agent execution is unavailable” and approval is disabled while execution is unavailable.
issues.userImpact: Users cannot start, pause, cancel, retry, or approve a real long-running job.
issues.recommendedFix: Ship an isolated runner with authoritative persisted state, cancellation, recovery and truthful progress before enabling controls.

issues.title: Scheduled execution is unavailable
issues.description: Task authoring/history UI exists, but background execution is explicitly unavailable in this deployment.
issues.evidence: The rendered/source-backed operational notice says “Scheduled execution is unavailable” and “Background execution is unavailable in this deployment.”
issues.userImpact: A task can appear product-like without being able to execute on schedule.
issues.recommendedFix: Keep authoring disabled or clearly read-only until a scheduler, entitlement check, execution history and delivery path work end to end.

issues.title: Maps is an education preview, not a functional map response
issues.description: The route intentionally provides no map canvas, markers, directions, geolocation, or provider-backed fallback.
issues.evidence: Existing parity evidence explicitly documents that no map implementation ships.
issues.userImpact: Map queries cannot produce a current rich response equivalent.
issues.recommendedFix: Implement a licensed, privacy-reviewed provider and accessible list fallback, or remove Maps from product navigation and label it as documentation.

issues.title: Secure browser automation is unavailable
issues.description: The visible browser-run surface reports that isolated execution is being rebuilt.
issues.evidence: Visible unavailable copy is rendered by AgentWorkspace and the API returns browser_agent_unavailable.
issues.userImpact: Agent workflows that imply browser actions cannot run.
issues.recommendedFix: Do not expose creation controls until isolated execution, confirmation, audit trail, cancellation and timeout recovery pass browser E2E.

issues.title: Real checkout lifecycle is not end-to-end verified
issues.description: Pricing and return surfaces exist, but no test customer/payment method was used; failed payment, cancellation, downgrade, recovery and webhook-driven entitlement transitions were not rendered.
issues.evidence: Local source/tests can validate contracts only; they do not demonstrate a real Stripe lifecycle or production webhook state.
issues.userImpact: Users could see stale plan or entitlement information after payment events.
issues.recommendedFix: Run isolated Stripe test-mode journeys for success, abandonment, failure, cancellation, portal return and delayed webhook reconciliation.

issues.title: Role and tenant-isolation UX is not rendered under multiple principals
issues.description: Owner/editor/viewer, invite, restore and delete code exists, but the audit had no lawful multi-user seeded workspace to verify permissions and failure messages.
issues.evidence: No authenticated multi-principal storage states were available; local signed-out rendering is insufficient.
issues.userImpact: A permissions defect could expose data or misleading controls.
issues.recommendedFix: Seed two tenants and three roles; verify every control, direct URL, realtime update, invite expiry and ownership boundary.

issues.title: Real streaming interruption and provider failures are not end-to-end verified
issues.description: Source and synthetic tests cover error mapping, but no real provider stream was observed for partial tokens, stop race, retry, rate limit or mid-stream network loss.
issues.evidence: The local audit did not use production AI credentials and generation remains environment-dependent.
issues.userImpact: The primary workflow may fail differently under real network/provider timing.
issues.recommendedFix: Run staging provider tests with fault injection after first token, abort races, 429/5xx/timeouts and reconnect; assert persisted partial state.

issues.title: Image provider and moderation lifecycle is not verified
issues.description: The rendered generator surface exists, but no live generation/edit was completed for moderation rejection, unavailable provider, timeout, retry, history and mobile detail actions.
issues.evidence: No image-provider credential or production account was used in this audit.
issues.userImpact: The image surface may appear complete while its core value path is unavailable.
issues.recommendedFix: Exercise a staging provider with accepted, rejected, timeout, billing-limit and edit inputs across phone and desktop.

issues.title: Authentication recovery matrix is incomplete
issues.description: Signed-out forms render, but bad credentials, Google OAuth callback/provider outage, reset email delivery, expired links, MFA, returning sessions, switching and deletion recovery were not completed.
issues.evidence: Auth availability is configuration-dependent; authenticated release testing explicitly requires external state.
issues.userImpact: Users can be locked out or receive unverified recovery feedback.
issues.recommendedFix: Use a dedicated test auth project and disposable accounts to cover every transition and restore focus/error announcements.

issues.title: Connector lifecycle is only partially verifiable locally
issues.description: Google and GitHub surfaces expose setup and operational states, but OAuth consent, incomplete scopes, expiry, reauthorization, sync, revocation and provider outage were not run with real test accounts.
issues.evidence: Connector status can resolve to temporarily_unavailable; no external provider account was authorized.
issues.userImpact: Connection labels may diverge from actual provider state.
issues.recommendedFix: Build deterministic provider sandboxes/fakes plus one lawful staging OAuth matrix; verify scopes and server-authoritative state.

issues.title: No independently verified sandboxed code-execution workflow
issues.description: Files and rich rendering exist, but the audit found no completed hosted code execution with timeout, unsupported format, chart output and retry evidence.
issues.evidence: The route inventory has no dedicated execution surface; agent execution is unavailable.
issues.userImpact: Uploaded datasets may not deliver the familiar analysis workflow users expect.
issues.recommendedFix: Provide a resource-limited execution service, explicit supported formats, downloadable outputs and failure recovery, or truthfully label analysis as model-only.

issues.title: Artifact workflow lacks full end-to-end persistence/recovery proof
issues.description: Editing surfaces exist, but creation from chat, selection editing, version restore, Library save, Work/Research handoff and failure recovery were not all completed against persistent authenticated storage.
issues.evidence: The write route advertises local autosave; authenticated cross-surface persistence was not available.
issues.userImpact: Users may lose work or encounter handoffs that only partially persist.
issues.recommendedFix: Add a seeded E2E that creates, edits, restores, saves and hands off an artifact with injected storage failures.

issues.title: Ownership, large-file and unsupported-file behavior is unverified
issues.description: Signed-out/empty rendering does not validate uploads, extraction, removal, ownership isolation, quota, large files or unsupported media.
issues.evidence: Chat API explicitly handles extracted content being unavailable; no two-user upload matrix ran.
issues.userImpact: Users may assume attached content was read or may see confusing upload failures.
issues.recommendedFix: Run multi-user storage tests with boundary sizes, MIME spoofing, extraction failures, cancel/remove races and attach-to-chat.

issues.title: Temporary Chat and memory lifecycle is not end-to-end verified
issues.description: Memory UI/API exist, but add/edit/delete/search/use, disabled memory, Temporary Chat exclusion and provider-context effects were not observed under a signed-in account.
issues.evidence: The API has explicit temporary-summary guards, but no rendered authenticated proof was available.
issues.userImpact: Private memories could be omitted, overused or incorrectly retained.
issues.recommendedFix: Verify persisted memory across sessions and prove Temporary Chat makes no read/write calls, including disabled/offline/error cases.

issues.title: Assistant authoring and publishing parity is incomplete
issues.description: Browse/detail surfaces exist, but a full create/edit/knowledge/capabilities/share/publish/permission workflow was not demonstrated.
issues.evidence: Route inventory exposes list and detail but no verified end-to-end authoring/publishing journey.
issues.userImpact: Users lack proof that custom assistants can be safely authored and shared.
issues.recommendedFix: Either add server-authoritative authoring/publishing with visibility states and moderation, or label the directory read-only.

issues.title: Research success, partial, cancel and provider-failure states are not live-verified
issues.description: Planner UI and server gating exist, but a real cited report was not produced and interrupted research was not resumed or cancelled.
issues.evidence: Deep Research is paid/auth gated and the audit had no eligible authenticated state.
issues.userImpact: Citation trust and long-running research recovery remain uncertain.
issues.recommendedFix: Use an entitled staging account and deterministic search provider fault injection to test sources, partial persistence, cancel and retry.

issues.title: Automated smoke checks do not establish screen-reader accessibility
issues.description: Keyboard/focus checks and source contracts are useful, but no NVDA, VoiceOver or TalkBack session verified announcements, reading order, rich response semantics or dynamic errors.
issues.evidence: Available tests are browser automation; no assistive-technology transcript or device run exists.
issues.userImpact: Screen-reader users can still be blocked despite passing DOM assertions.
issues.recommendedFix: Run manual AT audits on primary journeys and record defects/transcripts; include forced colors, zoom and reduced motion.

issues.title: Device-browser and safe-area verification is incomplete
issues.description: Configured viewport emulation covers required widths, but it cannot establish iOS Safari keyboard resizing, Android IME, notches, dynamic viewport units or device font scaling.
issues.evidence: Playwright viewports are emulated; no physical-device evidence was produced.
issues.userImpact: Composer or sheets may be obscured on real phones.
issues.recommendedFix: Run iOS Safari and Android Chrome device tests with keyboard open, rotation, 200% text, safe areas and long content.

issues.title: Lovable-named routes remain in the shipped route tree
issues.description: Although not primary navigation, .lovable and /lovable compatibility endpoints remain publicly addressable, conflicting with a strict independent-of-Lovable product surface goal.
issues.evidence: Generated route tree includes /.lovable/oauth/consent and several /lovable/email/* paths.
issues.userImpact: Security scanners and users can encounter obsolete third-party naming.
issues.recommendedFix: Migrate consumers, return permanent tombstones without branding, then remove the compatibility namespace and generated routes.

issues.title: No voice conversation/read-aloud surface
issues.description: Voice-only capabilities are intentionally absent rather than falsely exposed. This is truthful but leaves a familiarity gap versus current ChatGPT.
issues.evidence: Tests explicitly enforce absence of speech-recognition and speech-synthesis UI.
issues.userImpact: Users requiring hands-free interaction lack an equivalent.
issues.recommendedFix: Treat as an explicit product decision; only add with consent, privacy, interruption and accessibility design.

issues.title: Advanced enterprise administration is absent
issues.description: Verified-domain, SSO/SCIM, groups, retention, audit export and company-knowledge administration are not complete product surfaces.
issues.evidence: The maintained parity gap report defers these features.
issues.userImpact: Enterprise buyers cannot self-administer identity and governance.
issues.recommendedFix: Add only after server-side authorization, audit and legal requirements are defined.

issues.title: Study is a focused prompt surface, not a verified adaptive study system
issues.description: The route provides a Kova equivalent entry point, but no live adaptive curriculum, progress memory, quiz lifecycle or learning-state recovery was verified.
issues.evidence: Only the route shell and navigation were locally inspectable.
issues.userImpact: The label may set expectations beyond a specialized chat preset.
issues.recommendedFix: Clarify capability copy or implement persisted plans, quizzes and progress controls.

issues.title: Operational status and support delivery are not production-backed in this audit
issues.description: Public pages render locally, but current incidents, support delivery, SLA language and response workflow were not validated against production systems.
issues.evidence: Local preview cannot prove live status telemetry or ticket delivery.
issues.userImpact: Users may not get actionable help during an outage.
issues.recommendedFix: Connect status to independent health telemetry and exercise support submission/delivery without exposing recipient data.

issues.title: Chromium browser-runtime expiry cleanup is timing-sensitive
issues.description: The three-engine browser-runtime suite failed its permission/expiry cleanup case only in Chromium: the session expired before the screenshot assertion, while the same case passed in Firefox and WebKit.
issues.evidence: npm run test:browser: 14 passed, 1 failed. Failure at tests/browser-runtime/runtime.spec.ts:102 raised BrowserRuntimeError: Browser session has expired.
issues.userImpact: Timing-sensitive session expiry can terminate a browser action before an expected artifact is captured.
issues.recommendedFix: Use a deterministic clock or TTL margin in the test and runtime; separately assert cleanup after artifact completion and rerun Chromium repeatedly.

issues.state: empty chat and composer text entered
issues.title: Release UI parity checks use stale or ambiguous selectors
issues.description: The required release-browser project failed all three tests at 320 px even though the captured composer visually displayed a send control. The top-bar locator matches both responsive DOM variants, and the visible send button lacks the test hook expected by the release contract.
issues.evidence: npx playwright test --config=playwright.release.config.ts --project=signed-out-chromium-320 --workers=1: 3 failed. .kova-topbar resolved to two elements; [data-testid=send-button] was absent after text entry. Failure screenshots and traces are under artifacts/release-browser-results.
issues.userImpact: The release parity gate cannot reliably distinguish a real responsive regression from a stale selector, so it cannot certify the product.
issues.recommendedFix: Use :visible or a single responsive header landmark, restore a stable semantic send hook on the actual button, and rerun all 24 signed-out engine/viewport projects without concurrency contention.

issues.title: Work route throws while rendering unavailable/history data
issues.description: The actual rendered crawl captured a repeated TypeError (`h.map is not a function`) from the Work bundle across 17 browser/viewport records. This is separate from the truthful runner-unavailable state.
issues.evidence: Rendered 365-record local crawl: 17 console TypeErrors from assets/work-*.js; all route navigations still returned below-400 HTTP status, showing why HTTP smoke alone misses it.
issues.userImpact: The Work surface may partially crash or hide history/results when an unexpected payload shape arrives.
issues.recommendedFix: Validate response schemas before rendering, normalize non-array payloads, show OperationalState failure/retry, and add malformed-payload E2E fixtures.

issues.title: Audit log throws on a non-array payload
issues.description: The rendered crawl captured `TypeError: a.map is not a function` from the Audit Log bundle.
issues.evidence: Rendered local crawl console output from assets/audit-log-*.js at /audit-log.
issues.userImpact: An authorized user can receive a broken audit surface instead of an explicit backend failure.
issues.recommendedFix: Schema-validate the loader response and render a labelled error/retry state rather than calling map on unknown data.

issues.title: Rendered crawl found unnamed and undersized interactive elements
issues.description: The DOM audit found 28 unnamed visible interactive-element instances across six route/browser/viewport records and 1,794 instances below 24 px across repeated matrix records. Counts are instances, not unique controls, and require manual triage; they are not silently converted into an exaggerated defect count.
issues.evidence: Unnamed instances appeared on Apps (8 each at desktop and 375 px), Help (3 in Chromium/Firefox/WebKit), and the WebKit homepage (3). No document-level horizontal overflow was found.
issues.userImpact: Some icon/empty links may have no accessible name, and small interactive targets can be difficult for touch or motor-impaired users.
issues.recommendedFix: Export selectors from the crawl, remove duplicates, add accessible names, and make primary touch controls at least 44×44 CSS px without inflating inline text-link boxes.
